question: What happened on January 27, and why wasn't it counted?
answer:
**On January 27, Rowan was absent from the group.** The signed attendance record says, “Final roster confirms Rowan was absent for the entire group. No patient treatment contact occurred.” [BH-D108] It also records that staff left a scheduling message, with “no clinical discussion” [BH-D108].

| Record | What it shows | Why it was not counted |
|---|---|---|
| Group psychotherapy, contact `HG-M042/2026-01-27/HG-E116` | Marked **no-show**; patient not present; **0** minutes established. | The signed attendance record establishes no treatment contact occurred. |
| Scheduling outreach, contact `HG-M042/2026-01-27/scheduling_or_outreach#BH-D108:S2` | A message was left after the missed group. | It was scheduling outreach, not therapy; no clinical discussion occurred. |
| Draft and posted charge, document BH-D112 | The draft “was generated from the appointment template before the scheduled group” and had no clinician attestation or finalized patient-specific narrative. [BH-D112] A group-psychotherapy charge was posted. | The draft and charge do not establish that care occurred, so they do not override the signed no-show record. |

**Bottom line:** January 27 was excluded from therapy attendance and goal counting because the reliable attendance record documents a no-show, while the outreach was non-therapy and the draft/billing entry did not substantiate delivered care.
